name: Example: Calculating a Component of a Vector in the Kernel of a Linear Transformation
problem: Consider the linear transformation ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071281/assets/d0a0fabd7275cdceed8c0c62e58bbfc0e5f23322145d551e412877075cbb6e3c.png) and the vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071281/assets/4dd5f4c300c5870e696c5485fffdef1bbd9b7741b23c7d27fda1198e31baa33b.png) Find the value of $\,k\,$ such that $\,\mathbf{u}\in\textrm{Ker}(\mathbf{T}).$
worked_solution:
A vector $\mathbf{u}$ belongs to the kernel of a linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ if $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{u})=\mathbf{0}.$ 

So, we need to solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(u) & =0 \\ [\begin{aligned}3\cdot k+12\cdot 2-3\cdot 6 \\ -2\cdot k+4\cdot 2-2\cdot 6 \\ 6\cdot k-3\cdot 2+3\cdot 6\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}3k+6 \\ -2k-4 \\ 6k+12\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}3k+6=0 \\ -2k-4=0 \\ 6k+12=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to all three of these equations is $k=-2.$
